title: Jo’s setup note for the Maple Court seed swap
titleZh: 喬給楓庭種子交換會志工的準備便條
passage:
Before tomorrow’s swap, we still need to check the packet labels. Hold an ordinary print against an adhesive sheet at the window and look through both pages. The center cross on Ruth’s first test lined up with its gap, but each outside cross missed its gap, falling a little closer to the center of the sheet. Keep that page for comparison.

The filled packets are on the counter. Each still has its lot symbol written on the back. R is the early red bean; S has the same common name but different planting advice. We’ll keep “red beans” as the large sign for both. The handout gives planting advice in separate rows marked by lot symbol. We put name-only sample labels over the handwritten symbols on two practice packets. After taking them to another room with the handout, Mira said, “I think you’ve mixed up the advice.” The two rows were right; she simply couldn't tell which row belonged to which packet.

I expected to need another sample before closing, but Ed got a clean one from his laptop without editing the shared label file. He used the same printer and tray as Ruth and took the next sheet from the same pile. Both outer marks aligned on his sample. Keep his working setup as it is. Remember that moving the feed sideways shifts all the marks together. Each computer’s print window, on the other hand, can scale the page around its center before it goes to the printer.

One visitor is coming early just to see the actual seeds, not to take an exchange packet. If the counter is crowded, we can show her at the side table. The opened display envelopes serve that purpose; Ed moved their tray to the windowsill while we set the sealed exchange packets out on the counter. Please keep the exchange packets closed.

One last note on the labels: we also tried a sample with only the lot symbol. It worked once Mira had the handout, but at the mixed-crop pickup tray she asked, “Is this the bean I came for, or is it a pea?” Visitors often choose what they want from that tray before taking a handout. The printed labels will cover the handwritten marks. The pickup tray has no separate sections: volunteers refill it wherever a space opens. A packet’s paper tally band can carry a reference number, but volunteers remove it from each packet at the counter to count what has been taken. The adhesive label stays on the packet.
passageZh:
明天的交換會開始前，我們還要檢查種子包標籤。請拿一張普通紙樣張和一張背膠標籤紙疊在一起，對著窗戶看。露絲第一次試印時，中央的十字符號對準了間隙，但兩側的十字都落在各自間隙靠中央的一側，比應在的位置更靠近中央。請保留那張樣張，以便比對。

分裝好的種子包在櫃檯上，每包背面仍有手寫批次符號。R 是早熟紅豆；S 的俗名也叫紅豆，種植建議卻不同。兩批仍共用「紅豆」的大標牌。講義依批次符號分列種植建議。我們拿兩個練習用的種子包，把只寫俗名的樣張貼在手寫符號上。米拉帶著種子包和講義到另一個房間後說：「我覺得你們把種植建議弄反了。」兩列建議都沒有寫錯；她只是不知道哪一列對應哪一包。

我原以為關門前還得再印一張，但艾德沒改共用標籤檔，就用自己的筆電印出一張對位正確的樣張。他用的是和露絲同一台印表機、同一個紙匣，從同一疊紙再取一張。他印的樣張兩側標記都對準了。請維持艾德原本可用的設定。把進紙位置往側邊移會讓所有標記一起平移。另一方面，各台電腦的列印視窗可以在送印前以頁面中央為基準縮放。

有位來訪者會提早來，只想看種子本身，不是要領交換用的種子包。如果櫃檯太擠，可以在側桌展示給她看。已打開的展示袋是為此準備的；我們把密封的交換用種子包擺上櫃檯時，艾德已把展示盤移到窗臺。交換用種子包請不要拆封。

最後再補充一點：我們也試過只寫批次符號的樣張。米拉拿到講義後能查到對應的建議，但在放著各種作物種子包的領取盤旁，她問：「這是我要的紅豆，還是豌豆？」來訪者通常先從盤裡選種子，再拿講義。印好的標籤會蓋住手寫標記。 領取盤沒有分區；哪裡有空位，志工就把種子包補到哪裡。每包可用紙束帶標出參考編號，但志工會在櫃檯取下束帶統計領取量。背膠標籤則會留在種子包上。
